description: Substack fund letter — China cloud + AI monetization (mixed conviction)

input.name: Alibaba Group Holding
input.why_own_it: As the largest position in the fund (50%!), we need to discuss Alibaba's latest earnings, which left us genuinely conflicted. On the one hand, the earnings demonstrated the company's strength in Cloud, which grew 36% year-over-year, accelerating from 29% last quarter. In tandem, Alibaba is moving towards aggressive monetization of its AI portfolio by shifting from open-source to a proprietary paid enterprise model for its high-end tools: Qwen3.6-Plus. All of this is good news as it reflects significant momentum in cloud computing and monetization potential for AI products.

description: Substack fund letter — FCF/ROIC value pitch at $39.84

input.name: PayPal Holdings
input.why_own_it: We initiated a significant position in PayPal (Ticker: PYPL) at $39.84 per share. We first looked at the company in late 2023, shortly after Alex Chriss became CEO, when shares were near $60. The business had most of what we look for, but the valuation did not meet our margin of safety threshold. The roughly 40% price decline since then created a price we found compelling. The market is pricing PayPal as a business in structural erosion. That conclusion is not supported by the fundamentals. The company generates $5.6 billion in annual free cash flow, earns returns on invested capital above 20%, and yields roughly 15% on free cash flow at our purchase price.

description: Substack fund letter — duopoly + DSD moat thesis

input.name: Flowers Foods
input.why_own_it: Flowers is the second-largest packaged bread manufacturer in the U.S., behind Grupo Bimbo, forming a functional duopoly in a category with meaningful barriers to entry. The most important of these is its direct-store-delivery (DSD) network: nearly 6,000 distributor territories where independent operators own exclusive rights to deliver and merchandise products. This infrastructure is difficult to replicate and costly to rebuild.

description: Substack fund letter — Netflix margin expansion + valuation

input.name: Netflix
input.why_own_it: Looking at the financials, Netflix's trailing twelve-month (TTM) revenue grew by 16.7% year-over-year to $46.9 billion. Alongside this, its TTM operating profit surged by 25.2% year-over-year to $13.9 billion. The company is steadily expanding its profit margins, with the incremental profitability on its revenue growth comfortably outpacing its historical margins. At a share price of $87 and a market capitalization of $366 billion as of May 15, 2026, Netflix is trading at a forward multiple of 22.7x its operating profit (~$3.85 per share for FY2026E). In my view, this is a highly attractive valuation considering the vast runway of opportunities the company has over the coming decade.

description: Substack — messy small-cap deep value pitch, grammar slips intact

input.name: Richardson Electronics
input.why_own_it: When I bought shares around $11, RELL presented the best asymmetric opportunity I could find in the market with nearly 80% of its market cap in current assets and 20% net cash. The Q3 numbers basically validated my thesis strongly with the backlog growth and profitability. I think we will see $1-1.50 in run rate earnings potential over the medium to long term. So for a company that has been losing money for the last few years to show that earnings potential while historically trading around 20x+ earnings - you can see where they stock could be headed.

description: Substack — PDEX dual-catalyst Zimmer/Monogram supply deal

input.name: Pro-Dex Inc
input.why_own_it: When Zimmer acquired Monogram, PDEX effectively stumbled into becoming the exclusive supplier for Zimmer's new robotics product line, which is expected to start generating revenue by early 2027. This acquisition created a massive dual-catalyst for PDEX. First, as an early Monogram shareholder, they are receiving millions in upfront and ongoing cash payouts through Zimmer's CVR milestone structure. Second, through their supplier agreement, PDEX stands to realize >$100M+ in recurring annual sales as the robotics program ramps up—at gross margins substantially higher than their current portfolio average.

description: Substack — CareCloud FCF turnaround, new CEO trust
